en.title: Online Harassment, Threats and Blackmail: What to Do
en.directAnswer: Put safety first. Do not delete the messages or pay a blackmailer simply because they demand money. Save the full conversation, account links, dates, phone numbers and payment demands. If there is an immediate physical threat, sexual blackmail, child-related harm or extortion, seek police and legal help quickly.

en.lawMeaning: The current Cyber Security Act was amended on 1 July 2026. Any offence reference must be checked against the current consolidated text. This page gives a general route. A person’s exact rights can change because of facts, documents, deadlines, legal status, court orders or later amendments.
steps: Do not send more private material.
Do not pay without professional advice.
Tell a trusted person if safety is at risk.
Use police/cyber support for serious threats.
Preserve medical/financial evidence if harm occurred.
evidence: Full messages; URLs; screenshots; voice notes; phone; transaction demand; witness; police report number.
en.simpleExample: A blackmailer threatens to publish private photos unless money is paid. The victim should preserve the threat and seek help instead of sending more photos or money.
commonMistakes: Common mistakes: meeting the blackmailer alone.
Common mistakes: forwarding private images widely as “evidence”.

whatIf.answer: Save technical identifiers you have and report.
